_doc: Ratchet bounds for tests/test_universality.py.
Floors (generation only grows): generative_share, planes, trigger_fires, ablated_share.
Ceilings (replay only shrinks): residual, shallow.
Equality (ground truth, never moves): total -- the tune's own write count. A share
whose denominator can move is not a ratchet: #117's artifact briefly lost 6492 writes
from its books and every percentage rose. Asserted by ==, not by a bound.
Recorded context, asserted by nothing: observed_fires, trigger_share, recover_s.
Loosening a bound is a deliberate, reviewable diff line, not a refactor's side effect.
planes floors Coverage.planes generated-per-plane, so a gain in one plane can no
longer mask a loss in another; the key set is exact, because which planes exist is
fixed by the tune's emits rather than by how well they are recovered.
trigger_share was the floor until #119 and is now context, for the reason its own
predecessor observed_fires became context: its DENOMINATOR moves with progress. A
RAW-replayed byte carries no trigger and a generated one needs one, so explaining
9291 pulse writes raised Commando's fires 99294 -> 105944 while the generated count
held at 15000 exactly -- the share fell 0.1769 -> 0.1714 on a step that replayed 5.5x
less. trigger_fires (Coverage.triggers[0], the generated count) is the floor that
replaces it: verbatim replay generates none, so it cannot be gamed by generating less,
and it does not fall when the value domain explains more.
ablated_share is what tests/test_tracker.py used to hardcode as >= 0.80: the share of
the tune's writes the graph still makes once the RAW floor is emptied. It is NOT
generative_share -- it counts writes made, not positions agreed, and so overstates --
and it lives here so lowering it is a ledger diff rather than a quiet edit in code.
Shares are floored at 6dp, never rounded: 0.941925926 records as 0.941925, because a
rounded-up floor fails >= on the very run that measured it.

baseline.records: the delivered state, not a starting point: bounds re-measured after the note-reload object (§4m) and the spilled-row reading so their gains are held by CI
baseline.jitter: none: every figure reproduced exactly on two independent runs, so the bounds sit at the measured value with no margin

tunes.measured: §4m walks `ctr_551A` down from the pitch word the note-on reloads and the spilled row reads the declaration the arpeggio's `+12` lands in: freq 1600 -> 1628, residual 118 -> 90, share 0.956148 -> 0.964444. trigger_fires holds at 505 while observed fires rise 2046 -> 2593, which is the trigger_share row of _doc
tunes.frames_why: 400 is where each structure recurs rather than happening once: orderlist cursor $54EC takes 3 values (2 advances), pattern cursor $54EF resets twice, and the $10 pulse ramp runs segments of up to 24 emits at step 22 over bound 256 (2 full turns). At 200 each of the three occurs exactly once; the full tune's 11750 frames is ~236s and far too slow for CI

tunes.measured: freq 5024 -> 5048, residual 122 -> 98, share 0.988178 -> 0.990466, shallow unmoved at 938 (§4m's seed is a reload, so it adds no observed byte). recover_s 5.0 -> 2.2: `_refine_voice` no longer rebuilds a per-frame default it already has
tunes.frames_why: the 400-frame entry cannot see the pulse-width sweep at all: Commando's turning instruments enter around frame 800, so pw holds 407/485 = 84% at 400 and 708/844 = 84% at 700, then knees to 600/1008 = 60% at 800 and 900/2115 = 43% at 1200 before #119. Sweeping 400..11750, 1200 is the smallest count that registers work of this size. Costs 5.0s to recover, against ~200s at 11750

tunes.measured: the control tune moves for the first time: 978/2099 survive ablation against 929, all of it the spilled row -- Follin's pitch reads run past their own table too. It still keeps no accumulator any declaration reaches, so §4m recovers nothing here
tunes.frames_why: a second engine at the same frame count; mid-range share, so movement in either direction is visible where Commando's 0.99 has little room left. It carries no pw plane at all -- its 1170 residual is mostly filter 0/802 -- so it locks the planes Commando's entries cannot
